derivation: accusative case of G5485 (χάρις) as preposition;
def: through favor of, i.e. on account of
kjv: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully

occurrences.text: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.
For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles,
For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.
For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:
Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre’s sake.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.
These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.
